title: ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) Outpaces Stock Market Gains: What You Should Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: ON Semiconductor Corp. (ON) gained 1.53% to $73.12, outperforming the S&P 500's 0.41% gain. The stock has risen 2.92% over the past month. Analysts expect Q3 earnings of $0.88 per share (up 39.68% YoY) and full-year earnings of $3.21 per share (up 36.6% YoY). The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Forward P/E of 22.44, trading at a discount to its industry average of 31.16.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong year-over-year earnings growth of 39.68% expected, revenue growth of 10.02%, stock outperforming market indices, trading at a discount to industry peers (Forward P/E 22.44 vs. 31.16), and favorable PEG ratio of 0.59 indicate solid fundamentals and growth prospects.

title: Will NVTS' NVIDIA Partnership Strengthen Its 800V Strategy?
author: Na
description: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) partnered with NVIDIA to develop a 24-kW power delivery board that converts 800V DC to 12V DC in a single stage, eliminating intermediate conversion steps. This advancement supports NVTS' 800V strategy as AI data centers demand more efficient power solutions. However, NVTS faces strong competition from ON Semiconductor and STMicroelectronics, and trades at a significantly elevated valuation with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the NVIDIA collaboration demonstrates technological progress and market opportunity in AI infrastructure, NVTS is significantly overvalued (P/S ratio of 37.83X vs. industry average of 4.71X), carries a Zacks Value Score of F, and has a Hold rating. The company is also expected to report a loss in 2026.

NVIDIA's collaboration with NVTS on advanced power delivery solutions for next-generation AI systems demonstrates its continued leadership in AI infrastructure and commitment to improving data center efficiency.

ON Semiconductor is expanding its AI data center power presence with expectations for AI data center revenues to more than double in 2026 and silicon carbide revenues to grow nearly 60% year-over-year, positioning it well in the 800V architecture transition.

STMicroelectronics reported 50% year-over-year growth in AI-related segments and expects data center revenues to exceed $1 billion in 2026 and $2 billion in 2027, demonstrating strong momentum in AI infrastructure power solutions.

title: 4 High-Risk Stocks Built for Big Returns
author: Lee Samaha
description: The article highlights four high-risk, high-reward stocks: Agios Pharmaceuticals awaiting FDA approval for mitapivat to treat sickle cell disease; Navitas Semiconductor pivoting toward AI data centers and high-power chips; Joby Aviation developing eVTOL transportation services with autonomous capabilities; and Viking Therapeutics developing obesity drug VK2735 with potential in a multi-billion dollar market. All require patience but offer significant upside if their respective catalysts materialize.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: FDA priority review of mitapivat for sickle cell disease expected by Nov 1 represents a major catalyst. Approval would expand addressable market with Wall Street consensus projecting the drug contributing one-third of total revenue by 2030, providing significant upside potential.

Strategic pivot to high-margin AI data center and HPC chips with Nvidia partnership for next-gen 800V architecture launching 2027. Management projects SAM growing to $3.5B by 2030 with revenue potential from under $50M in 2026, though profitability requires patience.

Differentiated transportation-as-a-service model with recent autonomous flight demonstration shows progress toward FAA certification. Long-term potential for profitable recurring revenue from proprietary transportation network if certification and commercialization succeed.

VK2735 shows steeper weight loss velocity than competitor tirzepatide in phase 2 data with phase 3 trials underway. Even small market share of projected $80B tirzepatide market in 2030 would significantly benefit the $3.6B market-cap company.

Mentioned as competitive benchmark with blockbuster weight loss drug tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro). Motley Fool holds position and recommends the stock, but article focuses on it as market comparison rather than investment thesis.

Referenced as Navitas partner for power chip development and as beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout. Motley Fool holds position and recommends stock, but mentioned contextually rather than as primary investment focus.

title: Why Investors Need to Take Advantage of These 2 Computer and Technology Stocks Now

description: The article highlights two computer and technology stocks with positive Earnings Surprise Predictions (ESP): ON Semiconductor Corp.
